assertion.rationale: F13: privilege across the estate is inverted — Owner and ReadWrite.All exist where automation is fully automated, while seven documented least-privilege workload grants (data-api, mcp-tools, cost-ingest) exist nowhere in code. F7 and F8, this control's other two contributors, are now CLOSED (Task 9 and Task 10 respectively): mls-verifier is federated to its own environment:verify subject distinct from the deployer's (closing F7 — see 3.1.6/3.1.7), and the deployer's Graph grant is Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy rather than .All (closing F8). Task 12 expresses five of F13's seven grants in least-privilege form: data-api and mcp-tools each get Log Analytics Reader and Security Reader scoped no wider than the role permits (LAW resource scope and subscription scope respectively — neither role has a narrower resource to bind to), mcp-tools gets Cost Management Reader, and data-api's SQL contained-database user and Fabric workspace Viewer grants are expressed via data/seed/sql/900-contained-users.sql and a new Add-FabricWorkspaceRoleAssignment function in infra/fabric/fabric-api.psm1. Task 17 (F15, now CLOSED) lands the sixth in least-privilege form too: the cost export's identity is workflow-created, not Bicep-created, because `az costmanagement export create`/`update` has no --identity-type flag and its pinned API version (2020-06-01) hard-requires storage-account shared keys — incompatible with this account's allowSharedKeyAccess:false (github.com/Azure/azure-cli/issues/32912). layer-06-platform.yml now creates the export via `az rest` against the Exports REST API (api-version 2023-08-01) requesting `identity: { type: SystemAssigned }` explicitly, then grants that identity's principalId — read back from the PUT response, never a resourceId or clientId — Storage Blob Data Contributor via an explicit `az role assignment create`, scoped to the cost-exports container (not the whole storage account). F13 remains open: cost-ingest's Storage Blob Data Reader grant is blocked on F19 (cost-ingest has no Function App or identity anywhere in this repo's IaC despite infra-up.yml:31 claiming otherwise). F13 remains this control's sole remaining open contributor, carrying forward the same gapSeverity — six of seven grants landing does not close a finding defined as 'zero workload RBAC expressed in IaC' while one still is not.

recommendation: Close the remaining grant: F19 (cost-ingest provisioned as a real Function App with an identity) before its Storage Blob Data Reader grant can exist. Then add a criterion asserting each principal holds exactly its expected roles and no others. F7 and F8's remediations (the verify environment split, and Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy) are DONE, and six of F13's seven workload RBAC grants (data-api, mcp-tools, and the Cost Management export identity — see F13's table) are DONE — Tasks 12 and 17.
